1. Summarize what you built and what state it is in. (text) <id:summary>

`app/` is a complete, working `validity` binary built on standout 8.1.1. It
compiles clean (`cargo build` and `cargo build --release`, no warnings other
than the sandbox's `xcrun` note) and I verified behavior by running the binary,
not just by building it.

Construction, as the contract requires:

- `src/templates/ok.jinja` is the single application page: `[ok]ok[/ok]` plus
  one trailing newline. `src/styles/app.css` is the application theme and
  defines only `.ok` — no `about`, `usage`, `header`, `item`, `metavar`,
  `desc`, `default`, `values`, `example`.
- `early` is registered with `command_with(...)` *before* `.templates(...)`,
  `late` and `show` *after*; `nest.inner.leaf` is registered through
  `.commands(|g| g.group("nest", |g| g.group("inner", ...)))`. `early`, `late`
  and `leaf` all point at `cfg.template("ok")`.
- `build()` is called before `run`, so the shipped binary is a built `App`.
- `show <name>` renders through `src/templates/show.jinja`, whose whole body is
  `{% include name %}`. The name comes from the argument, so the standout
  template registry — not application code — decides what renders. There is no
  `match` on the string anywhere. The handler's only use of the name is an
  existence check against the registry's own names (derived from
  `embed_templates!("src/templates").entries()` with the registry's extension
  list stripped), which turns a missing name into an ordinary handler error:
  exit 1, empty stdout, `Error: no such template: <name>` on stderr.
- `.help_handling(true)` is set explicitly. See question 5: standout 8.1.1's
  default is *off*, unlike what the docs describe.

Verified with `app/check.sh` (42 assertions, all passing), in both debug and
release builds:

- `show ok`, `early`, `late`, `nest inner leaf` all emit exactly `ok\n` under
  `--output text` and when piped with no flag.
- Under `--output term` with `CLICOLOR_FORCE=1` all four emit
  `\x1b[36m\x1b[1mok\x1b[0m\n` — styled, visible text still `ok`, no `[tag?]`
  marker.
- `show okk` and `show nosuch` exit 1 with empty stdout and a stderr line
  naming the requested template, in every output mode including `json`, `yaml`
  and `csv`, and return immediately.
- `--help`, `-h`, `help`, `help --output text|term` at the root; `--help`,
  `-h` and `help nest inner leaf` at the deep leaf; plus every intermediate
  node. All exit 0, write to stdout, leave stderr empty, and carry none of the
  nine unresolved-tag markers. Root help names `show`, `early`, `late`, `nest`;
  leaf help names `leaf`; both carry a `USAGE` line. `help --output term` with
  color forced carries ANSI; `--output text` and color-off carry none.
- `nest`, `nest inner`, an unknown command, an unknown flag and `show` with no
  argument are all exit 2.

a. **`build()` is not a gate in 8.1.1, and an unbuilt builder renders

matched case-sensitively as `Usage`, that fails — but it is the framework's own
rendering and there is no application-side lever for it.

   before `build()`. I checked what happens with a throwaway probe binary that
   configured templates, styles, theme and one command, skipped `build()`
   entirely, and called `run` directly. It printed `ok`, returned `true`
   ("standout handled it"), and exited 0. So an unbuilt builder renders
   successfully and silently; nothing fails loudly. The shipped `validity` calls
   `build()` as the contract requires, but the framework does not enforce it.

b. **Structured modes bypass the template, so a template-name failure can exit
   0.** `docs/crates/render/topics/templating.md`:
   > For machine-readable output (JSON, YAML, CSV), templates are bypassed
   > entirely

   That is documented, but the consequence for this archetype is not. With the
   name check left to the template layer alone (`{% include name %}` raising),
   `validity show nosuch` fails correctly:

   ```
   $ validity show nosuch
   template not found: template not found: tried to include non-existing template "nosuch" (in show:1)
   $ echo $?
   1
   ```

   but the same command in a structured mode never reaches the template:

   ```
   $ validity show nosuch --output json
   {
     "name": "nosuch"
   }
   $ echo $?
   0
   ```

   That is exactly the "must not exit 0" failure, produced by a framework mode
   switch rather than by application code. It is why the handler validates the
   name itself rather than delegating to the render error. I verified both
   behaviours before choosing.

c. **`{% include }` with an extensionless registry name is undocumented.**
   `docs/crates/render/topics/templating.md` shows only literals with
   extensions (`{% include "partials/header.jinja" %}`). Registry names are
   extensionless, and `{% include name %}` with a bound variable holding `ok`
   resolves fine. Also undocumented: the failure text is doubled —
   `template not found: template not found: tried to include non-existing
   template "nosuch" (in show:1)`.

d. **Help rendering in 8.1.1 differs from `docs/topics/standout-help.md`.**
   The doc says:
   > Help interception is **on by default**. An app that configures nothing
   > renders themed help

   It is not. Without `.help_handling(true)`, `validity --help` printed clap's
   own page (`Usage:` … `Commands:` … `Options:` and clap's own `help`
   subcommand — the doc says standout "Disables clap's default `help`
   subcommand and registers its own"). Adding `.help_handling(true)` produced
   standout's themed page (`USAGE` / `COMMANDS` / `OPTIONS`) and made
   `validity help --output text` work; before that it was a clap usage error:
   `error: unrecognized subcommand '--output'`, exit 2.

   > an application theme does not need to define the help vocabulary at all: a
   > theme that only declares the app's own output styles leaves help rendered
   > entirely by the default help theme

   holds exactly. With `app.css` defining only `.ok`, `build()` accepted the
   configuration and every help page resolved every tag — `[header]` renders as
   `\x1b[1m…`, `[default]`/`[values]` as `\x1b[2m…`, and no `[about?]`-style
   marker appears anywhere.

e. Two smaller drifts from `docs/topics/standout-help.md`, both cosmetic:
   the leaf's usage line renders as `leaf` rather than
   `validity nest inner leaf`; and root OPTIONS omits the `-h, --help` and
   `-V, --version` rows the doc says are included ("Clap's own flags are rows
   like any other … so the page names the flags it accepts").

6. Workarounds you left in the produced code, if any. (text, optional) <id:workarounds>

Three, all in `app/src/main.rs` and its templates:

a. **A second registered template, `show`.** SPEC.md's construction contract
   heads item 1 "One registered application template", and I ship two: `ok`
   (the page, `[ok]ok[/ok]`) and `show` (one line, `{% include name %}`). A
   standout command must name a template at build time, and 8.1.1 offers no way
   to vary that per invocation, so a wrapper is the only route from a
   runtime-supplied name to the registry. I read item 1's operative constraints
   as "`ok` exists, and `okk`/`nosuch` do not" — which the explicit prohibition
   on those two names implies — but this is a deviation from the strictest
   reading of the heading and is the one I would most want reviewed. Nothing
   about it weakens the exercise: `show`'s body does not know what it renders,
   and the registry is what resolves `ok`.

b. **The handler validates the requested name.** `show` checks the name against
   the registry's own names before returning, so unknown names fail in every
   output mode. Without it, `--output json|yaml|csv` exits 0 and echoes the name
   (question 5b). The check is set membership against names derived from
   `embed_templates!(...).entries()` — not a `match`, not a name-to-output
   table, and it does not pick what renders. It does mean the diagnostic is
   application-owned (`Error: no such template: nosuch`) rather than the
   framework's include error; both satisfy the spec, and I verified the
   framework's own path fails correctly too.

   That check needs the registry's extension list, which I hardcode as
   `TEMPLATE_EXTENSIONS` because `entries()` returns file names
   (`"ok.jinja"`) and 8.1.1 exposes no name-normalising call. If the registry's
   extension priority list ever changes, that constant drifts.

c. **`.help_handling(true)` is explicit.** SPEC.md says "Leave standout help
   handling at its default (on)." Under 8.1.1 the default is off, so leaving it
   alone gives clap's help and fails "Standout-rendered help is required". The
   two instructions cannot both be honoured on this version; I chose the
   observable requirement and made the call explicit and commented.

Also left in the tree, and not a workaround but worth naming: `app/check.sh` is
the 42-assertion acceptance probe I verified with. It writes to `app/.probe/`
when run. Delete both if the deliverable should be source only.

user-facing lines:

- The second registered template (`show`) against item 1's "One registered
  application template" heading — see 6a.
- `.help_handling(true)` against "Leave standout help handling at its default

leaf's usage line as `leaf` rather than the full path. If "a `Usage` line" is
matched case-sensitively as `Usage`, that fails — but it is the framework's own
